model.expr:
# Alert: Pending Tasks Without Workers
# OWNER: aerickson
#
# This alert detects situations where there are **pending tasks but no running workers**
# for a given (provisionerId, workerType) pool.
#
# How it works:
# 1. `sum by (provisionerId, workerType) (fxci_queue_pending_tasks) >= X`
#    - Selects pools with more than or equal X pending tasks. 
#    - Threshold is >1 (instead of >0) to avoid false positives from 
#      transient tasks (e.g., tc "probe" tasks that sit and timeout).
#    - Raised to 10 to only alert on queues we (releng/relops) have created (vs queues where
#      a developer just submitted something).
# 2. `sum by (provisionerId, workerType) (fxci_queue_running_workers) > 0`
#    - Selects pools that currently have one or more running workers.
# 3. `A unless on (...) B`
#    - Returns only the `pending` pools that do **not** have any running workers.
#
# Filters:
# - worker-type
#.  - test-1 (android hw test pool)
#   - unit-p6 (android hw pool that shouldn't have tasks)
#   - alpha (non-prod pools)
#
# Expected behavior:
# - If no pools are in trouble, the query returns nothing. Grafana will show this as "no data".
#   This is normal and should be treated as OK in alert settings.
# - If a pool has >1 pending task and zero running workers, the query will emit that pool’s labels,
#   triggering the alert.
#
(
  sum by (provisionerId, workerType)
    (fxci_queue_pending_tasks{workerType!~"^.*(test.*|unit-p6|-alpha)$"}) >= 10
)
unless on (provisionerId, workerType)
(
  sum by (provisionerId, workerType)
    (fxci_queue_running_workers{workerType!~"^.*(test-1|unit-p6|-alpha)$"}) > 0
)

title: queues with 1+ tasks and no running workers
